en: n. a substance used to change the color of cloth, hair or other materials; vt. to change the color of something using dye; vi. to become a different color after being treated with dye
ex: She dyed her hair blonde for the summer.
她為了夏天把頭髮染成金色。

en: n. a set of instructions for preparing a particular dish; a method or formula for achieving something; a medical prescription
ex: This recipe calls for two cups of flour and three eggs.
這道食譜需要兩杯麵粉和三顆蛋。

en: vt. to do something wrong or illegal; to promise to do something; to give someone or something to be taken care of; to send someone to a mental hospital or prison
ex: He was arrested for committing a robbery.
他因犯下搶劫罪而被捕。

en: n. a very rich person who has at least a million dollars, pounds or other currency
ex: He became a millionaire by the age of thirty.
他三十歲就成了百萬富翁。

en: n. a warm bed cover made of two layers of cloth with soft material between them, usually sewn in patterns; vt. to sew layers together to make a quilt; vi. to make a quilt
ex: Grandma made a beautiful quilt from old pieces of cloth.
奶奶用舊布片縫製了一條漂亮的被子。

en: vt. to take legal action against someone in a court of law; to ask someone formally for something; vi. to take legal action
ex: She decided to sue the company for unfair dismissal.
她決定控告公司不當解僱。

en: vt. to throw small drops or pieces of something over a surface; to scatter things here and there; vi. to rain lightly; n. a small amount of something scattered over a surface
ex: She sprinkled sugar on top of the cake.
她在蛋糕上撒了一些糖。

en: n. the act of persuading someone to do or believe something; the power to persuade; a set of beliefs, especially a religious or political group
ex: It took a lot of persuasion to get him to agree.
費了很大的勸說功夫才讓他同意。

en: v. to see or show the difference between two things; to be a mark or characteristic that makes something different; to see or hear something clearly
ex: It's hard to distinguish identical twins.
同卵雙胞胎很難分辨。

en: n. the fact of being male or female, especially as it relates to social and cultural differences; (in grammar) a class of nouns such as masculine, feminine or neuter; vt. to give a gender to something
ex: Employers must not discriminate on the basis of gender.
雇主不得以性別為由歧視。

en: n. an agreement in which a company promises to pay money if something bad happens; the money paid for this agreement; protection against loss or damage
ex: I need to renew my car insurance this month.
我這個月得續保汽車保險。

en: n. goods carried on a ship, plane or large vehicle
ex: The ship was carrying a cargo of oil.
那艘船載運一批石油。

en: n. a statement that you do not agree with something or are against it; a reason for not liking something; a formal statement that you oppose something
ex: I have no objection to your plan.
我對你的計畫沒有異議。

en: vt. to send back light, heat or sound from a surface; to show or be a sign of something; to think carefully about something; vi. to think deeply about something
ex: The lake reflected the mountains like a mirror.
湖面像鏡子一樣倒映出群山。

en: n. a deep spoon used for serving food such as ice cream; a piece of exclusive news published before other papers; vt. to pick up something with a scoop; to publish news before others
ex: She scooped some ice cream into a bowl.
她舀了一些冰淇淋到碗裡。

en: n. the legal status of belonging to a particular country; a group of people with the same culture, language and history; the quality of being a nation
ex: What is your nationality?
你的國籍是什麼？

en: n. the state of being perfect; the act of making something perfect; the highest standard of quality
ex: She works hard to achieve perfection in everything she does.
她在所做的每件事上都努力追求完美。

en: a. not extreme; reasonable and fair; of medium size or amount; vt. to make something less extreme; vi. to become less extreme or severe; to lead a discussion
ex: He has moderate political views.
他的政治觀點很溫和。

en: n. a person who starts an organization, institution or company; vi. (of a ship) to fill with water and sink; vi. to fail completely; vt. to cause something to sink
ex: He is the founder of a famous software company.
他是一家知名軟體公司的創辦人。

en: n. a person or company that makes goods in large numbers in a factory
ex: The company is the world's largest manufacturer of smartphones.
這家公司是全球最大的智慧型手機製造商。

en: n. a state of peaceful agreement and cooperation; a pleasant combination of musical notes played together; a pleasing arrangement of parts
ex: The neighbors live together in harmony.
鄰居們和睦相處。

en: n. the series of events that form the main story in a book, film or play; a secret plan to do something bad; a small piece of land used for growing plants or building; vt. to make secret plans; to mark a position on a map or graph; vi. to plan secretly
ex: The plot of the movie was too complicated to follow.
這部電影的劇情太複雜了，很難跟上。

en: n. a round handle on a door or drawer; a round control on a machine such as a radio; a round lump on a surface or tree; vi. to have a round lump; vt. to equip something with a knob
ex: He turned the knob and opened the door.
他轉動門把，打開了門。

en: n. a play in which most of the words are sung to music with an orchestra; a building where operas are performed; a style of musical drama
ex: We went to the opera to see Carmen.
我們去歌劇院看《卡門》。

en: n. a person whose job is to watch swimmers and rescue them from danger; a soldier whose job is to protect an important person; a bodyguard
ex: The lifeguard blew his whistle when the swimmer went too far.
游泳者游得太遠時，救生員吹了哨子。

en: n. a state of confusion or lack of order; a medical condition that stops part of the body or mind from working normally; a disturbance of public order; vt. to put something into confusion
ex: His room was in complete disorder after the party.
派對後他的房間一片混亂。

en: n. a set of numbers or symbols that expresses a mathematical rule; a method or plan for achieving something; a set of words used on a particular occasion; baby milk powder
ex: The scientist used a formula to calculate the speed.
科學家用了一個公式來計算速度。

en: vi. to fall suddenly and awkwardly; to roll over and over; (of prices) to fall suddenly; n. a sudden fall or roll; the action of rolling over
ex: The child tumbled down the stairs but was not hurt.
孩子從樓梯上滾下來，但沒有受傷。

en: n. the physical parts of a computer; tools and equipment used in the home or garden; heavy machines and weapons
ex: We need to update our computer hardware.
我們需要升級電腦硬體。

en: n. a section of writing that begins on a new line and deals with one main idea; a short article in a newspaper; vt. to divide writing into paragraphs; vi. to write short items
ex: The first paragraph introduces the main topic.
第一段介紹了主要主題。

en: n. a person who works with you, especially in a profession or business
ex: I had lunch with a colleague from the marketing department.
我和一位行銷部的同事一起吃午餐。

en: n. the process of judging how good, useful or valuable something is; a judgment about the value or quality of something; the act of calculating a value
ex: The teacher gave each student a written evaluation.
老師給每位學生一份書面評量。

en: n. the act of keeping something safe from harm or decay; the process of protecting food from going bad; the state of being kept in good condition
ex: The preservation of old buildings is important to the city.
保存老建築對這座城市很重要。

en: n. the act of printing and selling a book, magazine or newspaper; a book or magazine that has been published; the act of making information known to the public
ex: The publication of her new novel is planned for next spring.
她的新小說預定明年春天出版。

en: n. a person who is not brave and is easily frightened; a person who runs away from danger
ex: He was called a coward for running away from the fight.
他因逃離戰鬥而被稱為懦夫。

en: vt. to form or make up something; to be considered as something; to establish something legally; to appoint someone to a position
ex: Women constitute more than half of the workforce.
女性占勞動力的一半以上。

en: n. a politician in charge of a government department; a priest in some Christian churches; an official representing a government in a foreign country; vi. to take care of someone; to help a person or group
ex: The minister of finance announced the new budget.
財政部長宣布了新預算。

en: n. a person you spend time with or travel with; a person employed to live with and help someone; a thing that goes with another; vt. to go with someone or accompany them
ex: The old man's only companion was his dog.
老人唯一的伴侶是他的狗。

en: n. a type of job that needs special education or training; a statement of belief or feeling; a group of people who do the same type of work
ex: She chose teaching as her profession.
她選擇教書作為她的職業。

en: n. the act of refusing to accept someone or something; the state of feeling that you are not wanted; the act of saying no to a proposal or offer; the body's refusal to accept a transplanted organ
ex: She received a rejection letter from the university.
她收到了大學的拒絕信。
